questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
It was crucial that it was an English-speaking country so that I was able to communicate eaily with people in and outside class while still being challenged on an English academic level. 
Furthermore, it was an advantage that it was possible to get the erasmus grant when studying in Edinburgh as it helped a bit economically.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was as easy as it could possibly be I would say - the University itself was good at offering information through e-mail communication and so, and offering assistance if worried or in doubt.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved the possibility of joining a zoom(or so)-meeting with a little presentation about and introduction to University life with a possibility of questions. Also, there were several welcoming events which you could join via an app on your phone such as 'get to know each other' and a 'showing around campus' that was a bit helpful when arriving at a place where you have never been before.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy for me although I might have been lucky. I found my private housing (with three other international students) through the website Spareroom that I was recommended through someone who had been an exchange student in Edinburgh herself. For me, it was a really good experience to live in private housing because it was more homely than what I have heard about student acommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to know that the housing was not a scam (which can sometimes happen when you don't know much about a city and the living conditions), but my landlord validated herself right away through a website where I could check the validity of her being a lessor which might be a good idea to do.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration itself was easy because I just had to either participate in a welcoming online call or show up at the counter of the receiving student office. After that, I just had to show up to classes in which we were registrated every time with signature.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The office for recieving students at my college (College of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences) were always helpful with answering e-mails or you could show up in person after booking a meeting even though they were quite busy and you might have to wait a week or so for an answer.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of things that was difficult to find out through the online registration before arriving in Edinburgh and took a lot of time. I didn't even know my classes before arriving and starting at the University and couldn't recieve many of my first priorities courses, but as soon as it was finalized (after a period where everyone needs to be in contact with the same people who have to contorl your choice of classes) everything was fine and easy - although it was frustrating within the first two weeks.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient, you might not have an overview ready for all of your classes before arriving but you will figure it out eventually and people are always very helpful although they are busy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a mix of levels that i recieved though my courses. Some where first year classes which was interesting because I chose different causes than what I knew from home and practiced my academic English a lot, even though the level was a bit below where I am in my studies. Others were very challenging academically which I learned a lot from and were very happy to be a part of.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The two institutions have a lot in common - for example very intersting, skilled professors. But there was a bit more mixing of class types with both big lectures (where the professor is the only one speaking), smaller seminars where it is a lot of discussion between professor and students and lastly tutorials that are even smaller groups of students with becoming-professors. Also, the classes were often only one hour long which made it a bit more superficial but also more dynamic in the everyday school life.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Scottish Literature 2B
Critical Practice: Prose
Critical Practice: Performance
Poetry, Politics and Place

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Scottish Literature 2B and Poetry, Politics and Place were especially giving.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Unexpected costs were trips around the country: transportaiton, commodation and stuff.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and living (drinks) were a bit mroe expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A very nice Gym through the University. Furthermore, a lot of different societies (almost everything you can imagine).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Film society, hill hiking society and the Pleasence Sport Complex

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the Scottish Highlands (it is amazing) and take some trips to Glasgow by bus.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy and smooth - people are very polite and welcoming in Scotland.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a society or two, maybe find a private housing to live in with other students (that was helpful for me).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness, the welcoming attitude and a bit less stress than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join a society, go to the Scottish Highlands (and Glasgow) and use the unviersity's spaces for studying/reading/doing assesments/drinking with your friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be a part of a different culture/everyday life in a very easy nice way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting socially and getting to know the university system for classes and assesments.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
